meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Spain (national unitary jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction for the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (continental system), EU-harmonised corporate and AML legislation, notarial authentication and commercial registry registration model

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo (arts. 3, 4, 14, 30 and 32), as amended; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010 (arts. 21–42); Orden JUS/319/2018, de 21 de marzo, por la que se crea el Registro de Titularidades Reales; Real Decreto 609/2021, de 20 de julio, por el que se crea el Registro Central de Titularidades Reales; Regulation (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843 (4AMLD/5AMLD) as transposed and subsequently amended.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (with obliged-entity professional access): the Registro Central de Titularidades Reales is not fully public; access is granted to judicial, law-enforcement, supervisory authorities and to obliged reporting entities performing customer due diligence, pending the EU Single Access Point public-access reforms applicable from 2024–2027.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the foreign corporate shareholder's Certificate of Incorporation and constitutional documents (charter/statutes)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry or Companies House of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille certificate; for non-Hague-Contracting States, consular legalization at the Spanish Consulate plus official sworn translation into Spanish

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / certificate of no bankruptcy for the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of origin or Chamber of Commerce of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, with sworn translation (traducción jurada)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (Poder) appointing the Spanish incorporation attorney and company secretary for the notarial deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, followed by sworn translation into Spanish

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport/identity copies of all directors and of every individual holding 25% or more of the Spanish SL (UBO identity evidence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin (certified true copies)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, with sworn translation where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO statutory declaration (declaración de titularidad real) detailing the full ownership chain and ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign notary or, alternatively, executed before the Spanish notary at the incorporation deed stage
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if executed abroad; otherwise accepted as part of the Spanish notarial protocol (escritura pública)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference / banker's due-diligence confirmation letter for the foreign shareholder's corporate account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country bank branch or correspondent institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy without apostille; bank confirmation letter addressed to the Spanish notary; sworn translation if not in Spanish or English

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory identification and verification of all directors, shareholders and 25%+ ultimate beneficial owners against (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (Council Regulation (EC) No 881/2001 and Council Regulation (EU) No 2580/2001), (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List, (iii) the U.S. OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists, and (iv) the domestic Spanish sanctions listings and SEPBLAC circulars. PEP screening is mandatory under Ley 10/2010 art. 14 and SEPBLAC guidance; politically exposed persons trigger enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification and senior-management approval irrespective of the Low_Risk_Standard tier. For ISIC 4652 passive-electronics distribution, automated name-matching with manual resolution review is required, and all KYC/AML records must be retained for ten (10) years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central – Servicio de Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social, operated electronically through the Colegio de Registradores de España (www.registradores.org) and the certified digital 'certificación negativa' filing service; paper filing also accepted through any Provincial Mercantile Registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under arts. 404–408 and 411 of Real Decreto 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil), the company name may comprise words in any language only if written in Latin characters and capable of being read and identified in Spanish commercial usage without confusion; official filings and the notarial deed are in Spanish; the corporate-type suffix must appear as 'S.L.', 'S.L.U.', 'Sociedad Limitada' or 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada'; symbols, graphic signs, non-pronounceable strings, bare surnames (without consent) and names reproducing official public bodies are excluded.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: España / Reino de España (requires Council of Ministers authorization)
Mundial, Internacional, Europeo, Universal (require governmental or regulatory authorization)
Banco, Caja, Seguros, Reaseguradora, Mutua, Cooperativa, Sociedad de Garantía Recíproca (regulated financial and insurance terms requiring prior supervisory approval)
Gobierno, Ministerio, Ayuntamiento, Comunidad Autónoma, Estado, Administración, Agencia (false suggestion of public character)
Unión Europea, ONU, OCDE, Cruz Roja, NATO (international organisation denominations)
Names identical to existing companies or names presenting confusing similarity with a pre-existing registered denomination
Words, expressions or ideograms contrary to law, morality or public order (art. 407 Reglamento del Registro Mercantil)
Surnames of natural persons without the individual's express consent or, where applicable, without authorization of the Registro (art. 405 Reglamento del Registro Mercantil)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The negative-name certificate is valid for six (6) months from issuance; extension is obtained by filing a fresh application before expiry, thereby securing a further six-month reservation of the same denomination. Upon rejection, the applicant may (i) file a reconsideration request before the Registro Mercantil Central, (ii) lodge an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP, formerly DGRN) within one (1) month of notification in accordance with Ley 39/2015 (LPACAP), and (iii) contest a confirmed administrative denial before the Juzgado de lo Mercantil or the Contencioso-Administrativo chamber for the registered office domicile. To preserve incorporation momentum, the applicant may concurrently re-file a materially distinct denomination that avoids the rejected tokens.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permitted for a Low_Risk_Standard wholesale distributor of passive electronic components: a commercial virtual-office package providing a genuine Spanish physical address, mail handling, telephone reception, legal-address domiciliation and AEAT notification access may satisfy the registered-office requirement under art. 9 of Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010 (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), provided the address is not a mere PO Box, the management in fact directs operations from a verifiable location, and the notary and Registro Mercantil find no indicia of sham establishment. For tax substance, the AEAT requires that the place of effective management or a permanent establishment be verifiable in Spain; pure mail-forwarding without administrative or transactional substance is not per se sufficient and may trigger tax-residency or re-domiciliation challenges.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: approximately 5–10% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by the Agencia Tributaria (AEAT) or Social Security Inspectorate during the initial three (3) fiscal years for ISIC 4652 passive-components distribution with a Low_Risk_Standard banking profile. The probability increases to 15–20% where a virtual office is combined with large VAT refund claims, high-volume related-party cross-border transactions with Latin-American affiliates, or absence of substantive administrative records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), principally Articles 19-23 (formation and articles), 32-33 (registration and legal personality), 58-62 (capital contributions), 210-242 (administration), and 279-284 (annual accounts filing). Law 14/2013 and subsequent electronic formation rules may permit accelerated online processing. Law 18/2022 reduced the statutory minimum capital of a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada to EUR 1 and introduced additional creditor-protection rules while capital remains below EUR 3,000.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil) for the province of the registered office, under the coordination of the Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución) executed before a Spanish notary and filed for registration with the competent Provincial Commercial Registry, together with the certified articles of association and beneficial ownership information.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The minimum share capital is EUR 1. All subscribed capital must be fully paid at incorporation. Monetary contributions are normally evidenced by a bank certificate, although the founders may dispense with delivery of the certificate and assume statutory liability for the reality of the contribution under the Companies Act. No statutory escrow account is required; a dedicated pre-incorporation bank account is customary where a bank certificate is used. If capital is below EUR 3,000, the statutory reserve and creditor-protection rules applicable under Law 18/2022 must be observed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board resolves that: (1) the Company accepts and records the subscription and full payment of its share capital by the founding shareholder in accordance with the incorporation deed and articles; (2) the registered office at [full Spanish address] is adopted for all corporate and statutory purposes; (3) [name] is appointed sole director, or, if applicable, [names] are appointed joint or several directors, each accepting office and declaring no legal disqualification; (4) the appointed officer is authorized to obtain the tax identification number, complete Commercial Registry filings, open the corporate bank account, and execute all documents necessary to commence the Company’s business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), through its online name-certification service or an authorized notary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to five proposed names and request a negative name certificate. Ensure the selected name includes or corresponds to Sociedad Limitada, Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada, or S.L. The certificate should be issued in the founder’s name and remain valid for the statutory period; provide the original or electronically verifiable certificate to the notary.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney, if an agent submits the request
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected, submit an alternative name or correct the proposed name in accordance with registry objections. If the certificate expires, obtain a renewed certificate before signing the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporating Spanish notary and, where relevant, the Company’s bank and the competent tax administration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles covering corporate name, purpose, registered office, capital, share divisions, transfer restrictions, governance form, and financial year. Determine the ultimate beneficial owners and obtain foreign investor identification numbers where required. Subscribe and pay the capital in full. Obtain a bank certificate unless the founders use the statutory declaration dispensing with certificate delivery.
required_dossiers: Founder passports or national identity documents
Foreign identification numbers or applications, where applicable
Evidence of capital deposit or founders’ statutory contribution declaration
Registered-office title, lease, or occupancy authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure missing identification, beneficial ownership, capital, or address evidence before execution. If the notary identifies an unlawful corporate-purpose clause, replace it with a precise and legally permissible activity description.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public (notario) selected for the incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the public deed in person or through a properly legalized and, where necessary, apostilled and translated power of attorney. The notary verifies identity, capacity, corporate name, capital, articles, beneficial ownership, and legal compliance. Request electronic submission to the Commercial Registry and obtain the provisional tax identification number process through the tax authorities.
required_dossiers: Capital bank certificate or statutory declaration
Apostilled and translated powers of attorney, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct notarial observations, provide missing legalized documents, or execute a supplemental deed. If a power of attorney is defective, re-execute it before a Spanish notary or provide a compliant legalized instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company and Obtain Tax Identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) and the State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized incorporation deed electronically or through the notary. Pay applicable notarial and registry tariffs, which vary by document and capital. Submit the census registration and request the provisional or definitive tax identification number using the applicable AEAT form. After registration, collect the registered deed and update the tax identification status where required.
required_dossiers: Electronic or certified copy of the incorporation deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to a registry qualification notice within the stated period by filing a corrective deed, supplemental document, or legalized evidence. If rejected, request reconsideration or lodge the statutory appeal before the competent Commercial Registry authority or court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Post-Incorporation Governance and Operating Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT, the relevant regional employment authority, the General Treasury of Social Security, the municipality of the registered or operating premises, and the competent autonomous-community industrial authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Legalize corporate books electronically through the Commercial Registry, register directors and employees with the applicable authorities, obtain the required workplace risk-prevention arrangements, and complete municipal activity or opening formalities for the warehouse or office. Confirm whether the premises require a responsible declaration, prior communication, activity license, fire report, or environmental authorization.
required_dossiers: Social Security employer registration, if employees are engaged
Technical activity and fire-safety report, where required
Municipal responsible declaration or license application
Environmental screening or authorization documents, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Address municipal or regional technical observations through revised plans, supplementary certificates, or corrected responsible declarations. Do not commence activities requiring prior authorization until the relevant approval or legally effective filing has been obtained.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The industrial authority of the Autonomous Community in which the premises are located, together with the relevant municipal authority. For ordinary distribution of passive electronic components, no national manufacturing license is ordinarily required; additional regional registration may apply if the premises constitute a regulated industrial establishment or handle regulated equipment or waste.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal activity and opening authorization (licencia de actividad y apertura), or a municipal responsible declaration or prior communication (declaración responsable or comunicación previa), depending on the Autonomous Community, municipality, premises, and activity classification.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge (Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico), acting with the competent environmental authority of the relevant Autonomous Community.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt from project-level EIA for ordinary office and warehouse distribution of passive electronic components, provided no listed industrial project, major construction project, protected-site impact, hazardous installation, or material environmental transformation is involved. Screening under Law 21/2013 may be required if the facility falls within an annexed category or is materially expanded.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or material VOC emissions are normally expected from passive-component distribution. Maintain lawful sanitary and stormwater discharges, prevent releases to soil or drains, and comply with applicable municipal or regional discharge conditions. Segregate, label, store, and transfer packaging, electronic waste, batteries, oils, and hazardous materials through authorized waste managers under Law 7/2022 and applicable regional rules. Any generated emissions, noise, wastewater, or hazardous waste must meet the permit-specific limits imposed by the competent authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain or document municipal fire-safety compliance under the applicable Building Code, fire-protection rules, and local technical requirements, including emergency exits, extinguishers, fire compartmentation, signage, and emergency lighting. Where applicable, obtain a technical fire report and certificates for electrical and fire-protection installations. Verify structural floor loading and storage-rack safety for warehouse operations. Complete occupational risk assessment, prevention planning, worker training, personal protective equipment controls, emergency procedures, and workplace registration or notification requirements before commencing operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), through the Sede Electrónica de la AEAT. The competent tax administration is generally the AEAT; the Basque Country and Navarre have separate foral tax administrations for taxpayers within their respective territorial regimes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF), generally beginning with the letter B, through the Modelo 036 census registration process. The provisional NIF is normally requested during incorporation through the notarial and commercial-registry one-stop process and must be converted into a definitive NIF after registration with the Commercial Registry. A foreign shareholder or director without a Spanish tax number must generally obtain an individual or foreign-entity NIF as applicable. A non-resident entity carrying on business, holding Spanish tax obligations, or requiring Spanish VAT registration applies for an NIF through Modelo 036, submitting constitutional documents, evidence of legal existence, identification of directors or legal representatives, and evidence of authority of the Spanish tax representative where required. Foreign documents may require apostille or legalization and certified Spanish translation. For intra-EU transactions, the entity separately requests registration in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios through Modelo 036; the resulting Spanish VAT identification number is generally the NIF prefixed with ES and is validated through VIES. The entity must report changes in tax domicile, activities, representatives, VAT status, and census data through the applicable AEAT filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: There is no general United States-style check-the-box election for a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada. The SL is ordinarily subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax as a separate legal person. Available elections or applications may include the consolidated tax regime for qualifying corporate groups, the special regime for mergers, demergers, asset contributions and exchanges, the special regime for entities engaged in leasing residential property where statutory conditions are met, the Canaries tax regimes where geographically applicable, and the VAT special regime for groups of entities. A Spanish tax-transparent or pass-through treatment is not generally available for an SL merely by election. Anti-hybrid mismatch rules can deny deductions, impose inclusion, or neutralize duplicate deductions and imported mismatches under the Spanish implementation of ATAD rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA), Spain's VAT system, supplemented by customs duties and import VAT. The Canary Islands, Ceuta, and Melilla are outside the EU VAT territorial scope and apply distinct indirect-tax regimes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold applies for ordinary Spanish VAT registration. A business must generally register before commencing taxable activities, making taxable supplies, acquiring goods or services that create Spanish VAT obligations, or importing goods. The €10,000 EU-wide threshold for certain intra-EU distance sales and qualifying cross-border B2C digital, telecommunications, broadcasting, and electronically supplied services is not a general domestic VAT-registration threshold; eligible businesses may use the Union or Non-Union One Stop Shop where applicable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not currently operate a universal real-time pre-clearance system for all domestic invoices. The Immediate Supply of Information (SII) system requires qualifying taxpayers, including businesses with turnover exceeding €6 million, members of VAT groups, and entities registered in the monthly VAT refund regime, to transmit invoice-register data electronically to the AEAT generally within four business days, extended to eight business days for invoices issued by the recipient or a third party. Electronic invoicing is mandatory for specified public-sector transactions and is being expanded for private-sector B2B transactions under the Law on the Creation and Growth of Companies, subject to implementing regulations and phased effective dates. Spain's VERI*FACTU and invoicing-system integrity rules require compliant software controls, traceability, preservation, and anti-tampering features; the applicable technical and implementation timetable must be monitored before deployment. Basque Country and Navarre may impose additional regional systems, including TicketBAI or equivalent requirements, where the entity is subject to the relevant foral tax administration.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from mainland Spain or the Balearic Islands to destinations outside the EU VAT territory may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct input VAT, provided the statutory export conditions are satisfied and the exporter retains reliable proof that the goods left the EU. Direct exports require dispatch by or on behalf of the Spanish supplier; indirect exports generally require dispatch by or on behalf of a non-EU purchaser and compliance with the applicable passenger or commercial export procedure. Intra-EU supplies of goods may qualify for exemption with the right to deduct input VAT where the customer is VAT-identified in another Member State, the goods are transported to that Member State, and the supplier holds the required evidence and reports the transaction correctly. B2B services are generally located where the business customer is established and may be outside the scope of Spanish VAT rather than technically zero-rated; special rules apply to services connected with immovable property, transport, events, intermediaries, and use and enjoyment. Evidence must be consistent with customs records, commercial invoices, transport documentation, customer VAT data, and required VAT returns or recapitulative statements.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice identifying the Spanish supplier, customer, goods, quantities, values, and contractual delivery terms
Electronic export declaration submitted through the Spanish customs system, including the Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Customs exit confirmation or equivalent electronic evidence that the goods physically exited the EU customs territory
Transport evidence, such as bill of lading, sea waybill, air waybill, CMR consignment note, courier record, or carrier confirmation
Packing list and warehouse dispatch or delivery records where relevant
Proof of the purchaser's non-EU status or destination, where required by the applicable export procedure
Import or customs-clearance evidence in the destination country where available and commercially appropriate
VAT accounting records and relevant Modelo 303 and Modelo 349 support
Inward remittance or bank-payment evidence where used as corroboration; it is not generally a universal statutory substitute for customs exit evidence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain has no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline of 180 days for export proceeds. Export VAT exemption is vulnerable to assessment where the taxpayer cannot prove dispatch, transport, customer status, customs exit, or correct reporting. The AEAT may retrospectively deny the exemption, assess unpaid VAT at the applicable rate, recover improperly refunded or deducted input VAT, and charge late-payment interest. Monetary penalties may apply for incorrect, incomplete, or fraudulent tax returns, failure to issue or retain compliant invoices, obstruction of inspection, and use of false or unreliable evidence; serious or very serious infringements can produce percentage-based penalties linked to the unpaid or improperly refunded tax, with aggravation for concealment, repeated conduct, or fraudulent means. Customs infringements may trigger separate customs debt, interest, fines, and loss of simplified or authorized-economic-operator privileges. Deliberate tax fraud may also create criminal exposure where statutory criminal thresholds and intent requirements are met.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) exercises exchange-control supervision as an Eurosystem NCB, supported by the Secretaría de Estado de Comercio (Ministerio de Economía, Comercio y Empresa) for the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores and by SEPBLAC (Spanish AML/FIU) for banking onboarding oversight. The legal liberalization framework is EU Art. 63 TFEU, Royal Decree 1816/1991 (operaciones de pago con el exterior), RD 571/2023 (foreign investment registry) and Ley 10/2010/RD 304/2014 for AML-KYC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a full Eurozone member; the euro is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. No exchange control authorization or central-bank permit is required for an ES_SL to receive export proceeds, inject foreign equity, pay foreign suppliers, remit dividends or repatriate capital. The only binding compliance layers are statistical declarations to Banco de España (Form TE for individual cross-border flows at or above EUR 50,000, filed monthly within the first ten business days), the ex-post registration of foreign direct investment (D-1A form to the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores within one month; prior-to-execution filing applies where the investment amount exceeds EUR 3,000,000) and the EU foreign investment screening regime (RD-Law 34/2020), which does not affect ISIC 4652 electronic-components wholesale because it is outside the critical-infrastructure, dual-use or national-security sector list. Profit remittance and dividends face no FX hurdle; the paying Spanish bank may only ask for evidence of tax residence, a solvency certificate and an anti-money-laundering source-of-funds update before executing repeated remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no export-proceeds surrender rules and no mandatory conversion ratio into EUR; this was abolished by the 1991 liberalization. An ES_SL may collect and retain export proceeds in any convertible currency, including USD or CNY, in accounts held at Spanish credit institutions or abroad. Reporting obligations apply only for statistical consistency: individual export-collection transactions equal to or greater than EUR 50,000 must be reported via Form TE to Banco de España within the first ten business days of the month following receipt; lower-value goods flows are captured by the customs SAD declarations. There is no time limit within which receivables must be repatriated, provided the company complies with transfer-pricing (Article 16 LIS) and Spanish controlled-foreign-company rules under the General Tax Law (LGT).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EUR multicurrency) + Restricted Capital Contribution Escrow + Trade Finance/Credit-Line Facility (Póliza de Crédito)
Operational Account (EUR/USD/CNY) + Capital Escrow Account + Import/Export LC and Forfaiting Line
Operational Account (SEPA and SWIFT) + Restricted Capital Account + Recourse Factoring Line
Operational Account + Capital Contribution Escrow + Short-Term Working Capital Credit Line
Operational Account (multicurrency) + Investment-Deposit Restringido + FX Forward/Swap Desk with Credit Support

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Conditional — rated Low as a sole treasury spine and Medium as a supplementary settlement overlay. Spanish-licensed or passported EMIs (Electronic Money Institutions) operating under PSD2 and supervised by Banco de España can open transactional EUR/GBP/USD accounts for an ES_SL without a physical branch visit, with e-KYC under RD 304/2014, and can provide cheaper MT103-correspondent-grade payments and FX conversion for the passive-components distribution flows. Legal constraints are material: EMIs are not credit institutions and cannot issue commercial documentary letters of credit, open aval-backed credit lines, provide bank guarantees, or supply a T2/TARGET2 direct settlement relationship; they are subject to frequent liquidity-raising limits and AML de-risking for electronics-wholesale business models; their ledger platforms are rarely ISO 20022 compliant for full supply-chain finance interoperability. Therefore, a fintech EMI is viable only as a second payment rail for Latin American receivables and USD disbursement optimization, while the primary corporate banking relationship must remain with a tier-1 Spanish bank able to offer the 'Credit_Line' target rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid statutory practice under Ley 10/2010 and RD 304/2014. Remote electronic identification is legally available only where the signatory uses a qualified electronic certificate (EIDAS) or a Banco de España-accredited video-identification process, but the prevailing tier-1 Spanish bank standard for an SL with non-resident shareholders requires at least one first-person KYC interview of a signing director or the attorney-in-fact at the branch. A public deed of appointment of the representative (escritura de poder) legalized with The Hague apostille or by the Spanish Consulate is mandatory; certified Spanish translations are required for all corporate documents. For a foreign beneficial owner without a Spanish NIE/TIE, the bank ordinarily demands an in-person onboarding session and physical inspection of original passports, UBO declarations and invoicing contracts. An all-digital opening is practically feasible only for a company whose administrators hold DNIe/foreign eIDAS and whose UBO chain is composed of NIE-registered residents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO-déclaration opacity: non-resident shareholders, chain of corporate nominees, absence of natural-person identification above 25%.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized Certificado de Titularidad Real issued by the Registro Mercantil; full multi-tier ownership charter up to the ultimate natural person or a listed-company exemption; apostilled passports and NIE/TIE of each ultimate beneficiary; a Board resolution confirming the 25% threshold test under Article 4.2 of Ley 10/2010; Spanish legal opinion confirming absence of nominee or fiduciary arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dual-use and export-control red flags on multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCC, HS 8532.24.00) and resistors (HS 8533.21.00), potentially classified as restricted strategic or military-grade goods.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EU Dual-Use Regulation 2021/821 Annex-I self-assessment confirming commercial grade; component technical data sheets (X5R/X7R/C0G dielectric types, voltage ratings, package sizes) proving non-military specifications; ECCN classification from US origin exporters (EAR99); REACH/RoHS/EN 62368-1 certificates of conformity; end-user and end-use declarations from LatAm and EU buyers; signed non-embedded-weapons or non-military-end-use representation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Grey-market and excess-inventory suspicion: invoice pricing materially below manufacturers' list price, high stock turnover, vague description of 'excess electronic inventory'.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete provenance chain: original purchase invoices from franchised distributors or authorized EMS excess-stock programs; batch-level traceability registers (lot codes, date codes, OEM part numbers); Customs import SAD documents and TARIC codes; commercial correspondent contracts showing a 18-30% gross margin; ISO 9001:2015 quality certificate and inspection reports from third-party testing houses; insurance coverage for stored inventory; annual financial statements evidencing economic substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment-flow anomalies: rapid round-tripping to Latin America, unusual creditor jurisdictions, large cash-collateralized wires inconsistent with the low-risk electronics-wholesale profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved customer/vendor KYC file for every counterparty; distribution agreements with 30-90 day payment terms; Pro-forma invoices and packing lists for each wire; SWIFT GPI end-to-end tracking; a 12-month rolling cash-flow forecast aligned with the inventory purchase pipeline; annual Form TE declaration to Banco de España demonstrating that all external transactions are statistically reported; a formal SEPBLAC-compliant internal AML manual and a designated compliance officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity contribution from the non-resident shareholder: the Spanish SL first opens a restricted capital escrow account ('Cuenta de Integración de Capital') at a tier-1 bank; the shareholder sends an MT103 SWIFT wire in EUR using the beneficiary IBAN and Field 70 purpose text 'Direct foreign investment — share capital subscription — ISIC 4652 / HS 8532.24.00 — wholesale of passive electronic components'; the bank issues a capital-disbursement certificate to the notary; the notary completes the incorporation deed (escritura de constitución) and files the D-1A investment-registration form with the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores where the investment exceeds EUR 3,000,000 (smaller amounts are registered ex-post within 30 days); Banco de España statistical reporting applies through Form TE for any capital inflow >= EUR 50,000. Shareholder loan routing: execute a written intercompany loan agreement at arm's length, send MT103 with Field 70 'Shareholder loan — Article 16 LIS — non-resident direct lending — interest at market rate'; the Spanish bank requires the loan contract, the Form TE declaration and, where the lender is a connected party, a transfer-pricing benchmark. Verification requirements: bank confirms no shell-bank involvement, sanctions-screening of all ordering correspondents, and cash-flow consistency with the commercial activity described in the AML dossier. All EUR inbound non-SEPA flows arrive via TARGET2/SWIFT; euro-area intra-EU contributions use the SEPA Credit Transfer rail at no correspondent cost.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For European and EUR-based supplier settlements: SEPA Credit Transfer or Instant SCT, plus the T2/TARGET2 high-value rail for amounts above EUR 100,000. For Asia-Pacific, LatAm and USD/CNY/JPY inventory purchases: SWIFT MT103 wire with a clearing correspondent bank; Field 70 must reference the underlying purchase order and invoice. Commercial letters of credit are issued as irrevocable LCs under UCP 600 via SWIFT MT700, with confirmation bank delivery in Japan, Korea, Taiwan or mainland China; negotiation and maturity payments are routed through MT754/MT400/MT910 reimbursement instructions. The 'Credit_Line' target rail is structured as a bilateral póliza de crédito (revolving working-capital facility) secured against MLCC/resistor inventory, covering up to 80% of approved purchase invoices, plus a documentary-import line supporting the issuance of LCs and standby LCs for inventory acquisition. For remittance to Latin American distributors, prefer MT103 with correspondent routing through US clearing banks or new-generation SWIFT Go to reduce fees; goods-export settlements must be reconciled with Form TE monthly filings. All disbursements must maintain a clear ISO 20022 structural reference: Unique End-to-End ID, instructed amount, beneficiary BIC+IBAN and correct purpose code (e.g., 'Trade in goods — electronic components' / 'Commercial credit — import/export financing').
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX — EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, EUR/JPY — executed at the treasury desk with DVP settlement inside T2/TARGET2 and CLS for eligible pairs.
Outright FX Forwards (deliverable, tenor up to 12 months) under ISDA 2002 / FX Global Code, with CSA or credit-line collateralization; used to hedge USD/CNY payable and receivable windows.
FX Swaps (swap de divisas) for rolling overnight liquidity between EUR and USD without disturbing the LC collateral block.
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) to hedge long-dated USD supplier financing versus EUR revenue streams.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (EUR/CNH, USD/BRL, EUR/VND as applicable) under EMTA/ISDA 1998 NDF terms, solely for currencies with restricted onshore delivery; permissible as hedging only and requires EMIR NFC- status reporting.
Vanilla European FX Options (call/put on EUR/USD or EUR/CNY) for costless-collared conversion of excess-electronics-inventory sale proceeds; subject to MiFID II appropriateness assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Accounts with Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 4 months after the end of the financial year (30 April for calendar year ending 31 December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to 300,000 EUR and potential administrative dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Modelo 347 - Annual Declaration of Operations with Third Parties
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 20th day of the month following each quarter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines ranging from 60 to 600 EUR per omission plus late payment surcharges

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 20 July following the end of the calendar financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to 1,000 EUR or higher for late filing, plus interest and penalties

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit required if the company exceeds two of the following three criteria: net turnover exceeding 4,000,000 EUR, total assets exceeding 2,000,000 EUR, or average number of employees exceeding 50
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (PGC) or International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as applicable

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Beneficial ownership details must be registered and updated in the Registro Mercantil upon changes including share transfers; the annual accounts filing confirms the current structure

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general CIT (Impuesto sobre Sociedades), art. 29.1 Ley 27/2014 (LIS); reduced 15% for newly created entities in the first two tax periods with a positive tax base (art. 29.3 LIS) subject to activity and legal-form requirements.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Potential deductions: R&D&I tax credits (25%/12% under art. 35 LIS), reinvestment of extraordinary income (art. 42 LIS), digital transformation incentives, and export/foreign-investment support programmes. For a passive component distributor, the 15% new-business rate is the main available reduction; no specific sectoral credit applies.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (no year limit); offset restricted to 70% of current-year taxable base generally, 50% for taxpayers with net turnover >= EUR 20 million, and subject to a minimum annual offset of EUR 1 million (art. 26 LIS).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 200 (Modelo 200) filed electronically via the AEAT (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria) online portal, typically by a tax representative or via third-party software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month post-close date. For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, the due date is 25 July of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Contabilidad del ejercico: 'Resultado contable' (Net accounting profit/loss before tax).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the company's statutory accounting profit per the audited annual accounts; for non-resident-owned SLs, reconcile with Spanish GAAP if foreign GAAP was used for external reporting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Diferencias permanentes - aumentos aplicados sobre el resultado contable (Permanent differences increasing the tax base).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report any non-deductible expenses (e.g., 5% dividend participation exemption, representation expenses over limits, donations). Non-resident shareholders should ensure arm's-length transfer pricing adjustments are not erroneously treated as permanent differences.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Diferencias temporales - aumentos (Temporary differences increasing the tax base, e.g. depreciation with tax-effect).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include consolidation adjustments or accelerated depreciation; in an SL distribution business, focus on undue provisioning or inventory write-downs that require timing differences.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compensación de bases imponibles negativas de ejercicios anteriores (Loss carryforward offset).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply available prior-year negative tax bases subject to the 70%/50% limit (see above) and the minimum EUR 1 million rule. Maintain traceable loss completion schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Base imponible (Net taxable base after all adjustments).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the core line for tax computation. Non-resident parent companies must ensure transfer pricing documentation supports the resultant taxable base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tipo de gravamen (Applicable CIT rate; 25% general, 15% if newly established).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select the correct code; for new SLs, verify the availability of the 15% rate and record the period of entitlement.
Calculated as taxable base times rate. No manual adjustment; system-computed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deducciones, bonificaciones y pagos a cuenta (Credits, bonuses, and tax prepayments).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim applicable R&D or double-taxation credits. Non-resident parents should reconcile any foreign tax credits (DTA relief) here for  Brazil/LatAm operations as applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Retenciones y pagos fraccionados (Withholdings at source and installment tax payments).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Spanish source WHT suffered and quarterly installment payments made. Non-resident-owned SLs must coordinate WHT on interest/royalty payments with Form 193 annual returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resultado a ingresar / a devolver (Final tax due or refund).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If refund claimed, verify bank account in Spain or foreign account with NIF; non-resident entities often use a Spanish tax representative for refund administration.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without notification: 5% surcharge on the resulting tax due, increasing 1% for each full month of delay (max 20%). If no tax due, fixed penalty of EUR 200. Filing after official notice: 20% penalty. Delay beyond 12 months adds late-payment interest. Additionally, incorrect return due to neglect may incur penalty of 15% per art. 27 LGT.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% under Spanish Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR, art. 25.1) generally. For EU/EEA recipient companies meeting the Parent-Subsidiary Directive conditions (5% or 10% holding? actually 5% under current law) and holding the shares for at least 12 months, the rate is 0% (exemption). For non-EU/EEA, treaty rates may reduce the 19% (e.g., 0% under certain DTAs with substantive holding thresholds).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Step 1: The non-resident beneficial owner must obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from its home jurisdiction. Step 2: Deliver the TRC and a Form 210 self-declaration (or the entity may apply treaty relief at source via Form 211) to the Spanish payer before the payment date to apply the reduced rate. Step 3: If excess WHT was withheld, the non-resident must file Form 210 within four years from the end of the withholding year to claim a refund. For EU companies, a simplified refund procedure under the Interest/Royalties and Parent-Subsidiary Directives is available through the Spanish 'Procedimiento para la no retención' using form 211 and proof of EU parent status.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory IRNR 19% (EU/EEA residents with information exchange) / 24% (non-EU/EEA without DTA); treaty rates generally range 0%–15% (e.g., many DTAs provide 10%). Royalties: statutory IRNR 24% (non-EU/EEA) / 19% (EU/EEA residents with info exchange); reduced to 0% under EU Interest & Royalty Directive when certain shareholding and 24-month holding tests are met. Treaty rates for IP royalties commonly 0%–10% (depending on the royalty category), subject to TRC and beneficial-ownership requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full Local File and Master File (Datos Maestros and Datos Locales) are required if the Spanish entity's net turnover is >= EUR 10 million (art. 18.3 LIS). Regardless of turnover, a contemporaneous record (simplified) must be maintained for all cross-border related-party transactions. Country-by-Country Reporting applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue >= EUR 750 million.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: TNMM / Transactional Net Margin Method (Margen Neto del Conjunto)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not apply dedicated Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) similar to offshore jurisdictions, but the general anti-abuse rule (cláusula antielusión, art. 15 LIS) and substance-over-form doctrine (art. 13 LGT) allow the tax authorities to disregard artificial transactions lacking commercial justification. A 'shell company' with no employees, premises, or management in Spain may be reassessed as a foreign permanent establishment or a non-resident entity, denying treaty benefits and triggering 19% (or 24% for non-EU) WHT on deemed Spanish-source income. Substantiation of substance: lease agreement for a local office, payroll for at least 1–2 full-time staff, board minutes in Spain, and a genuine inventory-holding activity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting sales from the electronic inventory distribution business, invoicing without selling goods, or using fake supplier invoices to reduce the taxable base. For passive component distributors, failing to declare inventory purchases in Spain or parking profits in a low-tax jurisdiction without commercial substance triggers this offence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty under General Tax Act (LGT) arts. 184-190: proportional sanction of 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, plus late-filing/or interest. Criminal offence under Criminal Code (CP) art. 305: if the defrauded quota exceeds EUR 120,000, imprisonment of 2 to 6 years and a fine of up to sextuple the defrauded amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held jointly and severally for civil debts (art. 42 LGT and 367 LSC). Criminal liability: personal imprisonment of directors who ordered or tolerated the evasion; travel bans and revocation of tax ID numbers possible during investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an SL without any physical premises, employees, or active management; acting solely as a conduit for intercompany invoices for multilayer ceramic capacitor/resistor distribution. The company is formally valid but lacks substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may characterize the SL as a letterbox entity, denying CIT treaty benefits and levying a 15% (or 24%) withholding under IRNR on all invoiced amounts deemed distributed from Spain to the foreign parent. Additionally, an administrative penalty of EUR 1,500 to EUR 30,000 for obstruction of controls (art. 203 LGT) may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed AEOI declarations or banking arrangements knowing the lack of substance may face civil joint liability for the tax shortfall (up to the company's unpaid tax) and possible criminal accomplice liability under art. 305 CP. In serious cases, the court may issue a temporary ban on leaving Spain.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving wire transfers or credit-line payments without identifying the beneficial owner, ignoring the client’s industry (electronics distribution) or structuring transactions to avoid reporting; failure to maintain a risk assessment for passive components (classified as low-risk but still subject to AML obligations).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SEPBLAC may impose fines from EUR 60,001 to EUR 1,500,000 (serious infringement) or up to EUR 5,000,000 or 6 times the laundered value (very serious). Public reprimand and potential suspension of activity for 1–3 years can be added.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members who knowingly allow third-party ownership structures without AML checks are personally liable for the fine (art. 58 Ley 10/2010) and may face imprisonment from 6 months to 3 years under art. 302 CP, plus a fine of up to triple the laundered assets and a travel-ban order.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Late Filing / Failure to File Form 200
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to submit the annual CIT return within the 25 July deadline (or applicable month) after the six-month post-close period; continuous refusal to file after official notice.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late filing without notification: 5% surcharge + 1% per month (max 20%) on tax due; if no tax due, EUR 200. If filed after official requirement, 20% penalty plus interest. Non-filing beyond 1 year: penalty of 20% and loss of ability to offset loss carryforwards; the tax debt becomes enforceable via attachment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who caused the omission are jointly and severally liable for the penalty and interest (art. 42.2 LGT). In cases of criminal bankruptcy, a court may order a ban on managing similar companies for up to 10 years and abroad restrictions (travel ban).
